title: Mass defect and binding energy
description: E = mc², the mass defect and binding energy from AME2020 atomic masses, and the binding-energy-per-nucleon curve that shows why both fusion of light nuclei and fission of heavy nuclei release energy.

sources.title: AME2020 atomic mass evaluation (IAEA Atomic Mass Data Center; W. J. Huang et al., M. Wang et al., Chinese Physics C 45, 030002–030003, 2021): the masses of ¹H, ²H, ³H, ⁴He, ⁵⁶Fe, ⁶²Ni, ²³⁵U, ¹⁴¹Ba, ⁹²Kr and the neutron in the course's data file
CODATA 2018 recommended values (NIST): 1 u = 931.49410242 MeV/c², 1.66053906660 · 10⁻²⁷ kg; c exact
Mass–energy equivalence (Wikipedia): Einstein's 1905 paper 'Does the inertia of a body depend upon its energy content?', 1 kg ≈ 9.0 · 10¹⁶ J
Nuclear binding energy (Wikipedia): definition, mass defect, ⁶²Ni 8.7948 MeV and ⁵⁶Fe 8.7906 MeV per nucleon, deuteron 2.22 MeV
Nuclear fission (Wikipedia): Hahn and Strassmann, December 1938 (published 6 January 1939); Meitner and Frisch's explanation and the name 'fission' (1939); about 200 MeV per U-235 fission
Lise Meitner (Wikipedia): 1878–1968, about 30 years with Hahn in Berlin, fled in July 1938, the Christmas 1938 explanation with Frisch, the 1944 Nobel Prize in Chemistry to Hahn alone, meitnerium
